title: Derived direct images and component units for total simplicial sites
statement:
Work with small sites and geometric morphisms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention, def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Let $\mathcal C_\bullet$ and $\mathcal D_\bullet$ be simplicial objects in the category of small sites and morphisms of sites [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], and let $h_n:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_n)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D_n)$ be induced by morphisms of sites commuting with the structure maps. The identity and composition laws of the structure morphisms, and the commutation of the $h_n$ with them, may hold through specified canonical isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle identities (as for sites of schemes over the terms of a simplicial scheme, where they come from identifications of iterated fibre products). The total sheaf topoi have objects families $F_n$ and maps $f_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_q$ satisfying identity and composition, and these data induce $h:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_{total})\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D_{total})$. Restriction $r_n$ of abelian sheaves to each component is exact and the family $(r_n)$ is conservative. In the bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$r_n Rh_*J\simeq Rh_{n,*}(r_n J),\qquad r_n h^{-1}K\simeq h_n^{-1}(r_nK).$$
Under these isomorphisms, $r_n(\eta_{h,K})$ is $\eta_{h_n,r_nK}$.

source.place: Tag 0D97, lemma-direct-image-morphism-simplicial-sites; Tag 09WG, lemma-restriction-to-components-site, together with the component sheaf description in lemma-describe-sheaves-simplicial-site-site and the adjunctions of lemma-morphism-simplicial-sites.

proof.text: By the total-site sheaf description, a sheaf is exactly a family of component sheaves with transition maps along every simplicial operator satisfying the identity and composition compatibilities. The component functors are therefore the restrictions $r_n$ in the new component-restriction lemma. That lemma gives the exact left adjoint formula, exactness of each $r_n$, and conservativity of the family: a map of total sheaves is an isomorphism exactly when all its component maps are isomorphisms.

For compatible site morphisms $h_n$, define the inverse image of a family by $(h^{-1}F)_n=h_n^{-1}F_n$; its transition map along $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$ is $f_\alpha^{-1}h_p^{-1}F_p\cong h_q^{-1}f'^{-1}_\alpha F_p\xrightarrow{h_q^{-1}F(\alpha)}h_q^{-1}F_q$, using the specified commutation isomorphism $f_\alpha^{-1}h_p^{-1}\cong h_q^{-1}f'^{-1}_\alpha$ (inverse images of $h_p\circ f_\alpha\cong f'_\alpha\circ h_q:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_q)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D_p)$), and the cocycle identities give the identity and composition compatibilities. Define $h_*G$ degreewise by $(h_*G)_n=h_{n,*}G_n$. For $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$, its transition map $f'^{-1}_\alpha h_{p,*}G_p\to h_{q,*}G_q$ is the $(h_q^{-1}\dashv h_{q,*})$-adjoint of the composite $h_q^{-1}f'^{-1}_\alpha h_{p,*}G_p\cong f_\alpha^{-1}h_p^{-1}h_{p,*}G_p\xrightarrow{f_\alpha^{-1}\varepsilon_p}f_\alpha^{-1}G_p\xrightarrow{G(\alpha)}G_q$, where $\varepsilon_p$ is the component counit. Taking component adjoints gives mutually inverse maps between compatible family morphisms $h^{-1}F\to G$ and $F\to h_*G$: a family $(F_n\to h_{n,*}G_n)$ is compatible with the transition maps exactly when its adjoint family $(h_n^{-1}F_n\to G_n)$ is, by naturality of the component adjunctions and the definition of the two transition maps; the two composites are the identity by the component triangle identities. Hence $h^{-1}\dashv h_*$ and $r_nh_*=h_{n,*}r_n$ on the nose, with the component units and counits. (Stacks proves the same in the strict case A via $v_{total}$, Tag 0D96, where $h_{total,*}$ is the system $(h_{n,*}F_n,h_{n,*}F(\varphi))$ and $h_{total}^{-1}$ its componentwise left adjoint.)

source.place: Tag 0D96, lemma-morphism-simplicial-sites (proof, case A: $h_{total,*}$ and $h_{total}^{-1}$ on systems and $(g'_n)^{-1}h_{total,*}=h_{n,*}g_n^{-1}$).

proof.text: Let $L\in D^+(\mathcal C_{total})$. The total site is a small site, so its abelian sheaves have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], and they are the modules over the constant integer sheaf, hence a Grothendieck abelian category [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] (likewise for each $\mathcal C_n$, $\mathcal D_n$, $\mathcal D_{total}$). By the bounded-below representative theorem choose a bounded-below complex $J$ of injective abelian sheaves on the total site with $QJ\cong L$; it is K-injective. By the component-restriction lemma every $r_nJ$ is a bounded-below complex of injectives on $\mathcal C_n$, hence K-injective, and since $r_n$ is exact it represents $r_nL$. By the underived identity $r_nh_*=h_{n,*}r_n$ of step 2, $r_n(h_*J)=h_{n,*}(r_nJ)$; the left side represents $r_nRh_*L$ ($r_n$ exact, applied termwise) and the right side represents $Rh_{n,*}(r_nL)$. This gives $r_nRh_*L\simeq Rh_{n,*}(r_nL)$; by the uniqueness of K-injective resolutions up to unique homotopy [lem-sp-kinjective-computes](1) it is independent of $J$ and natural in $L$.

source.place: Tag 0D97, lemma-direct-image-morphism-simplicial-sites (proof: K-injective representative, Tag 09WH lemma-restriction-injective-to-component-site, and Tag 0D96).

proof.text: The inverse image $h^{-1}$ of step 2 is exact: by the component-restriction lemma a sequence of total abelian sheaves is exact iff each restriction $r_n$ of it is (each $r_n$ is exact and the family is conservative, applied to the cohomology objects), and $r_nh^{-1}=h_n^{-1}r_n$ with $h_n^{-1}$ exact as the inverse image of a geometric morphism. Thus $h^{-1}$ is applied termwise to any representative of $K$, preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces $h^{-1}:D^+(\mathcal D_{total})\to D^+(\mathcal C_{total})$ by the universal property of the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Restricting the termwise identity gives $r_nh^{-1}K=h_n^{-1}(r_nK)$ on representatives, natural in $K$, hence the canonical natural isomorphism in $D^+$.

source.place: Tag 0D96, lemma-morphism-simplicial-sites (proof: exactness of $h_{total}^{-1}$ and $g_n^{-1}h_{total}^{-1}=h_n^{-1}(g'_n)^{-1}$); Tag 09WG part (1).

proof.text: The ordinary unit of $h^{-1}\dashv h_*$ is the family of component units, by the adjunction of step 2. Represent $K$ by a complex $K$ of total abelian sheaves on $\mathcal D_{total}$ and choose a K-injective resolution $h^{-1}K\to I$ with $I$ a bounded-below complex of injectives (step 3); the derived unit $\eta_{h,K}$ is represented by the composite chain map $K\to h_*h^{-1}K\to h_*I$. Applying $r_n$ gives $r_nK\to h_{n,*}h_n^{-1}(r_nK)\to h_{n,*}(r_nI)$, the first arrow being the component unit. By steps 3 and 4, $r_nI$ is a K-injective resolution of $r_nh^{-1}K=h_n^{-1}(r_nK)$, so this composite is the standard representative of $\eta_{h_n,r_nK}:r_nK\to Rh_{n,*}h_n^{-1}(r_nK)$, and its target is identified with $r_nRh_*h^{-1}K$ precisely by the comparison of step 3 (computed with $J=I$) followed by $Rh_{n,*}$ of the comparison of step 4. Hence, under these isomorphisms, $r_n(\eta_{h,K})=\eta_{h_n,r_nK}$ as morphisms of $D^+(\mathcal D_n)$; independence of the choices is [lem-sp-kinjective-computes](1).

(2) Step 5 represented the derived unit on a K-injective representative of K and used conservativity to get an equality; rewritten as K→h_*h^{-1}K→h_*I for a resolution I of h^{-1}K, whose restriction is the standard representative of η_{h_n}. Its blueprint via was missing the item in front; fixed. The new node is a genuine lemma (09WG+09WH) and strictly smaller than the item. I found no duplicate in the DAG. lean.note: Uses the published compatible-family presentation TotalSiteSystemData on actual abelian sheaf categories. The coherent morphism helper retains the component adjunctions and both coherence laws. The total adjunction is characterized by its component inverse-image transitions and units; its derived direct comparison is the canonical rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange, not an arbitrary natural isomorphism. The inverse comparison is the localization of the ordinary component comparison. Site-induced origin is explicit in pSite, qSite, hSite.
